explain: A skill packages instructions and resources for a task; a tool exposes an executable operation. The manifest records purpose and compatibility without granting permission.
steps: Define a narrow task description and entry resource. || Keep executable tools in a separate capability list.
name: skill-package

explain: Progressive disclosure loads only the instructions needed for the selected task. A concise catalog avoids sending every detailed package into every request.
steps: Select a matching task from metadata. || Load only its referenced instructions and retain the rest as discoverable metadata.
name: skill-disclosure

explain: Conflicting package instructions cannot override trusted host restrictions. The host evaluates a proposed operation against its own allowed scope.
steps: Record a tool request suggested by skill content. || Enforce the host capability policy before script or tool execution.
name: instruction-precedence

explain: Portable skill behavior needs explicit input/output contracts and version compatibility, while runtime adapters remain separate. Validation makes assumptions inspectable.
steps: Record the required input and expected output fields. || Check the host can supply the required tool capability before loading the package.
name: skill-contract
